item.text: {"category_edits":[{"category":"hyperparameter_tuning","rationale":"For all four category models, jointly shorten maxlen to 64, double batch size to 256 and raise learning rate to 1.4e-3. Shorter sequences offset the larger batch's computation; larger batches may reduce gradient noise while the increased learning rate supports fitting within the fixed update budget. Retain dropout 0.3, AdamW and existing weight decay. Existing checkpoint metadata and predictor loading propagate maxlen consistently. Preserve HSTU formulas, features, embeddings, readout, loss, seeds and training caps.","edits":[{"find":"LR = float(os.environ.get(\"HSTU_LR\", \"1e-3\"))","replace":"LR = float(os.environ.get(\"HSTU_LR\", \"1.4e-3\"))"},{"find":"BATCH_SIZE = int(os.environ.get(\"HSTU_BATCH\", \"128\"))","replace":"BATCH_SIZE = int(os.environ.get(\"HSTU_BATCH\", \"256\"))"},{"find":"MAXLEN = int(os.environ.get(\"HSTU_MAXLEN\", \"128\"))","replace":"MAXLEN = int(os.environ.get(\"HSTU_MAXLEN\", \"64\"))"}]}],"change_summary":"Jointly tune history length, batch size and learning rate across all four independent HSTU category models; existing metadata keeps inference consistent."}
